About Biloxi

Living in Biloxi

Biloxi sits on a peninsula between the Mississippi Sound and the Back Bay of Biloxi. It has French colonial roots and a long history as a seafood and shipbuilding town, and today it is also home to Keesler Air Force Base and most of the Coast's large casino resorts.

Housing runs from historic homes in east Biloxi to newer neighborhoods north of the Back Bay in the Woolmarket area. Being close to the water is part of daily life here, so flood zones and insurance are worth checking early.

Places to know

Around Biloxi

  • Biloxi LighthouseCast-iron lighthouse from 1848, standing in the median of US 90.
  • Ohr-O'Keefe Museum of ArtMuseum campus designed by architect Frank Gehry, honoring potter George Ohr.
  • Maritime & Seafood Industry MuseumThe story of Biloxi's fishing and boatbuilding history, at Point Cadet.
  • MGM ParkMinor league baseball stadium on the Back Bay side of downtown.
  • Mississippi Coast ColiseumConcerts, shows and the convention center on the beach.
  • Biloxi Bay BridgeUS 90 bridge to Ocean Springs with a walking and biking path.

Getting around

Roads and commute

US 90 follows the beach, Interstate 110 connects downtown to Interstate 10 across the Back Bay, and the Biloxi Bay Bridge leads east to Ocean Springs. Keesler Air Force Base is in the middle of the city.

Workers who live in Biloxi spend an average of 21.3 minutes getting to work, one way (Mississippi average: 25.6).

Near the water

Flood zones and insurance costs can change from one street to the next on the Coast. Look up any address on FEMA's flood map, and ask me for help getting insurance quotes before you make an offer.
